title.en: Ethanol, ethanoic acid, soaps and detergents

text.en: Vinegar on the kitchen shelf, hand sanitiser in your bag and the soap at the sink all contain carbon compounds. Their properties come from their functional groups, the alcohol group in ethanol and the acid group in ethanoic acid.

Ethanol C2H5OH is a colourless, highly inflammable liquid that mixes with water in all proportions.
On heating with concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K ethanol loses water to form ethene, which is dehydration.
Ethanol reacts with sodium to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas, and burns in oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water.
Ethanol is used in antiseptics and hand sanitisers, as a solvent, in antifreeze and in methylated spirit, rectified spirit and power alcohol.
Ethanoic acid, or acetic acid, CH3COOH, is a carboxylic acid with a sour taste and higher boiling point than the matching alcohol; on cooling it freezes to ice-like flakes called glacial acetic acid.
It is made by the oxidation of ethanol using alkaline potassium permanganate or acidified potassium dichromate.
Ethanoic acid reacts with active metals to liberate hydrogen and with carbonates and bicarbonates to give a salt, carbon dioxide and water with brisk effervescence.
It reacts with sodium hydroxide to give sodium ethanoate and water, and its sodium salt heated with soda lime gives methane.
Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long chain fatty acids made from a fat and an alkali by saponification; sodium hydroxide gives hard soap and potassium hydroxide gives soft soap.
Detergents are salts of sulphonic acids or alkyl hydrogen sulphates and, unlike soap, they can be used in hard water and acidic solutions.

problem.en: Write the balanced equations for ethanoic acid reacting with (a) zinc, (b) sodium carbonate and (c) sodium hydroxide.

why.en: A neutralisation reaction giving a salt and water.

text.en: In all three the salt formed is called an ethanoate (acetate).

prompt.en: A student has two colourless liquids, ethanol and ethanoic acid. Suggest a simple test to tell them apart.

requiredIdeas.en: Ethanoic acid gives brisk effervescence of CO2
Ethanol gives no effervescence with bicarbonate

commonMisconceptions.en: Both give carbon dioxide with carbonates

points.en: Ethanol: alcohol, reacts with Na, dehydrates to ethene, burns to CO2 and water.
Ethanoic acid: carboxylic acid, reacts with metals, carbonates and bases.
Soap = fat + alkali (saponification); NaOH gives hard soap, KOH soft soap.
Detergents work in hard water; soaps do not.
